title: review: D-fixkind: failure_kind classifies a 'review request_changes' hold with rejecting comments as code_defect so auto_fix_round files the routine review round
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label D-fixkind (added by the human 2026-10-02 16:05). Defect seen on T-1556: its security review T-1562 returned request_changes with two comments on orchestrator/spawn.py (in scope), the daemon held it 'review request_changes: T-1562 (request_changes)', and auto_fix_round logged 'automatic fix round escalated (unknown): unknown' instead of filing the routine round. Cause, orchestrator/failures.py failure_kind: after the conflict/environment/permissions/quota checks and the invalid_spec check (which already reads the rejecting review comments through _rejecting_reviews), it reads test ids from resume_hint.failures and returns 'unknown' when there are none. A review hold carries comments, not failing test ids, so it never becomes 'code_defect', and daemon.auto_fix_round's branch `kind == "code_defect" and reason.startswith("review request_changes")` is unreachable in practice (tests/test_daemon.py::test_auto_fix_round_on_review_comments_in_scope only passes because its held_for_fix fixture also plants resume_hint.failures with test ids).

Change (orchestrator/failures.py, failure_kind; locate by symbol):
1. Directly after the invalid_spec check and BEFORE the test-id read: if the hold_reason (the lowercased `reason` already computed) starts with 'review request_changes' and `comments` (the _rejecting_reviews result) is non-empty, return 'code_defect'. No rerun, no flaky probe: review holds never run tests.
2. Nothing else changes: a review hold with no readable rejecting review still returns 'unknown'; gate_red holds keep the test-id path, the flaky rerun and the quota logic; invalid_spec still wins when a comment says the spec contradicts itself or an acceptance cannot be met (it is checked first).
3. auto_fix_round (daemon.py) is unchanged: it already decides routine vs escalate from whether every rejecting comment names a path in scope; with kind code_defect the existing path files the round, and an out-of-scope comment still escalates as today.

Tests (SPEC RULE): tests/test_failures.py gets a unittest.TestCase method that builds a held execute task (hold_reason 'review request_changes: T-R (request_changes)', NO resume_hint.failures) with one rejecting review task (role review, inputs [task id], result verdict request_changes, one comment with a path and issue) in a scratch bus like the neighbouring tests, and asserts failure_kind returns 'code_defect'; a second task with the same hold but no review rows returns 'unknown'; a review comment whose issue says the spec contradicts itself still returns 'invalid_spec'. tests/test_daemon.py gets a method next to test_auto_fix_round_on_review_comments_in_scope that holds a task 'review request_changes: <id>' WITHOUT resume_hint.failures, with one rejecting review whose comment path is in scope, runs daemon.auto_fix_round(P.Pool()) and asserts exactly one fix round was filed with that review id in inputs and the comment text in the spec; and that with the comment path out of scope no round is filed and the task is escalated as today. Run tests/test_failures.py and tests/test_daemon.py in the foreground after committing; never background a command and never run the full gate.

Out of scope: daemon.py, spawn.py, bus.py. Rollback: git revert of the merge commit.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Every test named in the acceptance must exist in the diff; the gate checks for them by id.
acceptance: tests/test_failures.py::test_review_request_changes_hold_is_code_defect: passes: failure_kind returns 'code_defect' for an execute task held 'review request_changes: <review id> (request_changes)' with a rejecting review (verdict request_changes, one comment with path and issue) and no resume_hint.failures; returns 'unknown' for the same hold with no review rows; returns 'invalid_spec' when the rejecting comment says the spec contradicts itself

tests/test_daemon.py::test_auto_fix_round_on_review_hold_without_test_ids: passes: auto_fix_round files exactly one fix round (inputs include the rejecting review id, spec contains the comment text) for a task held 'review request_changes: <id>' with no resume_hint.failures whose rejecting comment path is in scope; with the comment path out of scope no round is filed and the hold is escalated as today

result.summary: The failures.py change matches the spec. The new check sits after the invalid_spec check and before the test-id read, and it requires the lowercased reason prefix and non-empty rejecting comments. Review holds with no readable review still fall through to 'unknown', and invalid_spec still wins. Both named tests exist and cover the three required cases plus the out-of-scope escalation. I did not run the tests, but the gate reports green. The tests leave one low-severity isolation gap.

comments.issue: The scratch bus patches STATE, TASKS and RUNS but not bus.LOCK, unlike BusSandbox in tests/test_bus.py, so the lock file stays on the shared harness root. It also never calls bus._close_db(), so the sqlite connection cached for the temp path is left open after the directory is removed. Use a tearDown/addCleanup that closes it, or reuse the BusSandbox pattern.

The out-of-scope case runs auto_fix_round a second time on the same bus. It does not assert that the first task's round count is still exactly one after that second call, so it does not check against a duplicate round.
